title: Chapter 8 – Tournament Technical Recommendations: Mock Exam

questions.text: What is the recommended minimum lighting level for a tournament playing area?
questions.explanation: As per Article C01.1, a minimum of 200 lux is recommended for the playing area, with no direct light causing glare on the boards. Good lighting is essential for fair play and correct scoresheet recording.

questions.text: What is the recommended king height for chess pieces used in FIDE events?
questions.explanation: As per Article C02.1, the king should be between 85mm and 105mm in height. The diameter of the king's base should be 40-50% of its height. Pieces should be of the Staunton pattern.

questions.text: What type of clock is mandatory in FIDE-rated events?
questions.explanation: As per Article C02.3, digital clocks are mandatory in FIDE-rated events. Analogue clocks may only be used in events without increment and only with specific approval.

questions.text: Where is the clock placed by default?

options.text: To the left of the player with the white pieces
To the right of the player with the black pieces
In the centre of the table between both players
At the discretion of the player with White

questions.explanation: As per Article C02.3, the clock must be placed to the right of the player with the black pieces unless both players agree otherwise or the arbiter decides differently.

questions.text: Who does the scoresheet belong to at the end of a game?
questions.explanation: As per Article C02.4, the scoresheet belongs to the organiser and must be handed in at the end of the game. Players may request copies of their scoresheets.

questions.text: What is the recommended square size for a tournament chessboard?
questions.explanation: Per Article C02.1, the recommended chessboard square size is 50mm to 65mm per square. The board size must be proportional to the piece size — the king's base should occupy 75–80% of a square.

questions.text: What must the playing hall temperature ideally be maintained at?

options.text: Temperature is not specified in tournament recommendations

questions.explanation: Per Article C01.1, the playing hall should be maintained at a comfortable temperature, typically 18–22°C. Extreme heat or cold can impair concentration and affect the fairness of the competition.

questions.text: Which of the following is a requirement for scoresheet design in FIDE events?

options.text: Must be printed on official FIDE watermarked paper
Must include space for player names, move numbers and a draw offer column
Can be any plain paper as long as moves are legible
Must be submitted electronically — paper scoresheets are not accepted

questions.explanation: Per Article C02.4, scoresheets must include spaces for player names, their federation, round number, board number, move notation, clock times, and a draw offer column. They must be legible and handed in after each game.

questions.text: What is required for the rest room and analysis area at FIDE events?

options.text: No rest area is required — players must stay at their board
A separate room away from the playing hall where players can relax
The analysis area must be in the playing hall for spectators to watch
Rest room and analysis area can be combined with the press room

questions.explanation: Per Article C01.2, FIDE events should provide a rest room separate from the playing hall for players to relax. Analysis of games in the playing area is forbidden, so a dedicated analysis area away from the boards is recommended.

questions.text: What is the recommendation for the noise level in the playing hall?

options.text: Background music at moderate volume is recommended to aid concentration
The hall should be kept quiet, with minimal disturbance to the players
Audience commentary is allowed as long as it is kept at a low volume
Noise level is not addressed in FIDE technical recommendations

questions.explanation: Per Article C01.1, the playing hall should be kept quiet to allow players to concentrate. Noise from spectators, commentary, or other sources should be minimised. The arbiter must act to address excessive noise.
